metadata.freshness: Pinned releases are metadata selections, not claims of native runtime qualification. APT explicitly follows Noble security/ABI policy. Brew versions record provider metadata and must be compared with installed/upstream during updates.

shared_runtime_retirement.noble_system: Distro Python3/venv/pip, coreutils/findutils/sed/grep/diffutils/procps and GTK/D-Bus/X11/audio/Vulkan ABI packages are shared host infrastructure, not disposable feature payloads.
shared_runtime_retirement.native_host: APT/Homebrew Bash and Zsh can remain the current login or rescue shell after profile disable. Git, GnuPG, OpenSSH, OpenSSL, CA certificates, curl and archive tools remain available for bootstrap, signing, recovery and verification; native coreutils/grep/sed preserve verifier prerequisites.
shared_runtime_retirement.lifecycle: Feature/source/configuration/frontend retirement does not imply removal of these native packages. Explicit package retirement reports retained-shared-runtime and preserves installed payload, provenance, services and user data; it must not report uninstall success or purge/autoremove foreign reverse dependencies.
shared_runtime_retirement.removable: Ordinary owned apps/tools, the scoped Homebrew OpenStack Python and project/global mise runtimes are not made permanently installed by this policy. Native apps may remove only their verified owned package when the provider's removal plan has no foreign collateral; artifact/mise retirement removes owned exposure while retaining versioned recovery payload.
